cases.sentence: В тот день, как Сергей Иванович приехал в Покровское, Левин находился в одном из своих самых ___.
cases.explain: «мучительных дней» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The day on which Sergey Ivanovitch came to Pokrovskoe was one of Levin’s most painful days. It was the very busiest working time, when all the peasantry show an extraordinary intensity of self-sacrifice in labor, such as is never shown in any other conditions of life, and would be highly esteemed if the men who showed these qualities themselves thought highly of them, and if it were not repeated every year, and if the results of this intense labor were not so simple.

cases.sentence: А он разрывает снопы, и что-то командует, и кричит на баб, и ___ поправляет ремень на маховом колесе.
cases.explain: «быстрым движением» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: (I doctored her, when the beam fell on her in the fire)” he thought, looking at a thin old woman who was raking up the grain, moving painfully with her bare, sun-blackened feet over the uneven, rough floor. “Then she recovered, but today or tomorrow or in ten years she won’t; they’ll bury her, and nothing will be left either of her or of that smart girl in the red jacket, who with that skillful, soft action shakes the ears out of their husks. They’ll bury her and this piebald horse, and very soon too,” he thought, gazing at the heavily moving, panting horse that kept walking up the wheel that turned under him. “And they will bury her and Fyodor the thrasher with his curly beard full of chaff and his shirt torn on his white shoulders—they will bury him. He’s untying the sheaves, and giving orders, and shouting to the women, and quickly setting straight the strap on the moving wheel. And what’s more, it’s not them alone—me they’ll bury too, and nothing will be left. What for?”

cases.sentence: А он разрывает снопы, и что-то командует, и кричит на баб, и быстрым движением поправляет ремень на ___.
cases.explain: «маховом колесе» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: (I doctored her, when the beam fell on her in the fire)” he thought, looking at a thin old woman who was raking up the grain, moving painfully with her bare, sun-blackened feet over the uneven, rough floor. “Then she recovered, but today or tomorrow or in ten years she won’t; they’ll bury her, and nothing will be left either of her or of that smart girl in the red jacket, who with that skillful, soft action shakes the ears out of their husks. They’ll bury her and this piebald horse, and very soon too,” he thought, gazing at the heavily moving, panting horse that kept walking up the wheel that turned under him. “And they will bury her and Fyodor the thrasher with his curly beard full of chaff and his shirt torn on his white shoulders—they will bury him. He’s untying the sheaves, and giving orders, and shouting to the women, and quickly setting straight the strap on the moving wheel. And what’s more, it’s not them alone—me they’ll bury too, and nothing will be left. What for?”

cases.sentence: Почерневший от липнувшей к ___ пыли Федор прокричал что-то в ответ, но все делал не так, как хотелось Левину.
cases.explain: «потному лицу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Fyodor, black with the dust that clung to his moist face, shouted something in response, but still went on doing it as Levin did not want him to.

cases.sentence: Подавальщик был из ___, из той, в которой Левин прежде отдавал землю на артельном начале.
cases.explain: «дальней деревни» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Fyodor came from a village at some distance from the one in which Levin had once allotted land to his cooperative association. Now it had been let to a former house porter.

cases.sentence: Левин разговорился с подавальщиком Федором об этой земле и спросил, не возьмет ли землю на ___ Платон, богатый и хороший мужик той же деревни.
cases.explain: «будущий год» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Levin talked to Fyodor about this land and asked whether Platon, a well-to-do peasant of good character belonging to the same village, would not take the land for the coming year.

cases.sentence: – Цена дорога, Платону не выручить, Константин Дмитрич, – отвечал мужик, выбирая колосья из ___.
cases.explain: «потной пазухи» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “It’s a high rent; it wouldn’t pay Platon, Konstantin Dmitrievitch,” answered the peasant, picking the ears off his sweat-drenched shirt.

cases.sentence: – Да так, значит – люди разные; один человек только для нужды своей живет, хоть бы Митюха, только брюхо набивает, а Фоканыч – ___.
cases.explain: «правдивый старик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, well, of course, folks are different. One man lives for his own wants and nothing else, like Mituh, he only thinks of filling his belly, but Fokanitch is a righteous man. He lives for his soul. He does not forget God.”
